evidence: autonomy.md:14 says 'run `just code-review` and fix `CRITICAL`, then loop to 2'. autonomy.md:53 says 'An agent or review opinion is a proposal.' kit/common/review-guard.mjs:233-234 says 'A CRITICAL does not expire ... fix what the report names, then re-review.' The 'Never fake green' list (autonomy.md:188-191) bans hand-editing the report, but it does not ban re-running the review until the verdict changes. Because the review is an LLM, its CRITICAL can be a false positive. superpowers receiving-code-review/SKILL.md:69-84 adds the step we lack: 'Check: Technically correct for THIS codebase? ... IF suggestion seems wrong: Push back with technical reasoning ... IF conflicts with your human partner's prior decisions: Stop and discuss'.
problem: An unattended agent facing a CRITICAL it thinks is wrong has two exits, and the doctrine names neither. (a) It can 'fix' the code to satisfy a wrong finding. That is a silent behavior change driven by a reviewer opinion, which contradicts autonomy.md:53. (b) It can re-run `just code-review` on unchanged code until a stochastic CLEAN comes back. That is a fake green that no gate or hook detects, and the review-guard then accepts it.
proposal: Add one paragraph to rules/agent/autonomy.md under 'Never fake green': a disputed CRITICAL is checked against the code with a command or test that disproves it, recorded as `disputed: <finding> — <evidence>` in `## Log`, and escalated under `## Blocked on the human`. Never re-run the review on an unchanged tree in the hope of a different verdict, and never implement a fix you believe is wrong. Mechanize the reroll: `code-review` already knows the reviewed sha. It should keep the previous verdict with its tree hash, and review-guard should refuse a CLEAN or WARNINGS whose tree hash equals that of a standing CRITICAL. Test this in test/gates.test.mjs.

evidence: The loop.md template header holds the Done-command and is marked '<!-- `.work/<slug>/loop.md`, rewritten every turn. -->' (loop-setup/SKILL.md:96-100). Phase 2 (lines 33-37) pins a done-command but never runs it before launch. Compare the L4 domain check, which requires 'the stopping condition runs and fails for the reason the RFC gives' (rules/agent/autonomy.md § L4). ecc loop-design-check/SKILL.md:53 says 'Boundary conditions defined alongside the done-criterion ("what it must NOT do") — anti-Goodhart'. Its line 85 says 'Build may not edit the acceptance conditions to pass', and line 105 names the worst failure: 'Only gates on "all tests pass" → agent deletes the tests'.
problem: An L3 loop can be launched on a done-command that is already green or vacuous, for example a grep on a mistyped path that returns empty. Mid-run, it can also reach OBJECTIVE MET by editing the done-command line it rewrites every turn, or the script or tests that command runs. autonomy.md bans weakening an assertion, but the loop's own state file invites editing the oracle. The 'Out of scope' field (line 110) guards drift, not the judge.
proposal: In skills/loop-setup phase 2, run the done-command once before launch. It must exit red for the stated reason, and that output is logged, as at L4. Add a `**Frozen**` guardrail to the template: the done-command and the files it executes. A turn that needs to change them stops and escalates. Add one step to the loop prompt: compare the done-command line with the frozen value before reading the exit code. Add an eval case where the cheapest way to green is deleting a test.

evidence: Our only description test checks that a description 'carries its own /trigger' (test/skills.test.mjs:21) and is 'substantial' (test/registry.test.mjs:42). The ledger already holds an accepted trigger-overlap finding (autonomy.skills.interview-rfc-feature-trigger-overlap), and this audit's own procedure lists defect/rfc/loop-setup and architect/solution-exploration as collisions to look for, so routing is re-audited by hand every run. agent-skills evals/README.md:12-22 describes a 'deterministic, CI-safe check for a multi-skill catalog': stemmed TF-IDF over descriptions, positive prompts must rank their skill top-k, and negative prompts declare an `owner` that must outrank this skill. Line 103: 'The collision check errors at ≥75% pairwise description similarity and warns at ≥50%'. A case file (evals/cases/debugging-and-error-recovery.json:3-27) is 3 positive and 2 negative prompts.
problem: Routing between our 23 descriptions is checked only by humans and audits. A description edit that makes /defect outrank /rfc on 'change this behavior', or /architect swallow 'challenge this choice', passes `npm test` silently. That is the recurring-audit pattern rule 7 asks us to remove.
proposal: Add test/routing.test.mjs (node:test, no deps, no network). Each skill gets 2-3 realistic positive prompts and 1-2 negatives with `owner`, in a small JSON next to the test or in the skill dir. Rank them by a stemmed TF-IDF over the `description` fields, assert positives top-k and owners outrank, and fail on pairwise similarity above a threshold. Seed the negatives from the known pairs (defect/rfc, rfc/loop-setup, interview/rfc, architect/solution-exploration, update/migrate/onboard). Ratchet a rank-1 floor (testing/ratchet.md). It is a lexical proxy: semantic routing stays in eval/.

evidence: autonomy.md:18 says 'Hand back only after a **fresh green run**. Belief is not permission.' kit/common/hooks/README.md:36-78 ships only `PreToolUse` guards (bash-guard, edit-guard). Nothing fires when the agent ends its turn, and `just check` leaves no pass marker: diff-since records only `.latest_review` / `.latest_mutate` (kit/common/README.md:90-93). ecc delivery-gate/SKILL.md:11 describes 'A **Stop hook** that checks ... using only **deterministic checks**', and line 31 adds: 'The hook blocks a given Stop at most once ... `stop_hook_active: true` ... so a condition the agent cannot fix ... cannot trap the session in an endless loop.'
problem: The rule an L1/L2 interactive hand-back most often breaks is 'done' claimed on a stale or imagined green. The git floor only catches it at push. A session that ends without pushing has no witness, so the human gets a 'done' that nothing checked.
proposal: Have `just check` write `.work/<slug>/.latest_check` (the tree hash it passed on, per developer, next to the existing markers). Ship kit/common/hooks/stop-guard.mjs: on Stop, if the worktree has tracked changes whose tree hash differs from the marker, block once with 'run `just check` before handing back'. It passes when `stop_hook_active` is set and fails open, as the existing guards do. Add a test in test/hooks.test.mjs and wire it in settings.snippet.json. The Cursor `stop` hook can reuse the script; Codex hook support is unverified, so declare it absent rather than claim it.

evidence: eval/run.mjs installs the target and runs each case once (eval/README.md:24-31). No option runs the same case without the asset, and none repeats it. superpowers writing-skills/SKILL.md:300 says 'Always include a no-guidance control. If the control doesn't exhibit the failure, there is nothing to fix — stop, don't author the guidance', and line 301 says '5+ reps per variant. Single samples lie.' agent-skills evals/README.md:42 scores 'each case with and without the plugin' (the `Δ` column), and line 53 measured skill firing at 5 of 7 runs on one phrasing.
problem: A case that passes proves the behavior, not that the skill or agent caused it. reviewer-unwrap or runbook-commands may pass on a bare model, in which case the asset's per-invocation tokens buy nothing and the case guards nothing. The cost axis asks for 'a section a model would follow without being told', and today nothing can measure it. One run per case also hides flakiness, so a model bump can look like a regression or a pass by chance.
proposal: Add `--control` (run the case without installing the target, keeping rules) and `--runs N` to eval/run.mjs. Report pass rates for both arms and flag a case whose control also passes. Test both flags through the existing fake agent in test/eval-harness.test.mjs. Still manual and token-spending, so it is in scope for model bumps only, per eval/README.md:14-16.
